h: A Geordie Night Out, Planned Properly
p: Before you head down, a few handy pointers. Book ahead, especially for weekend nights, and arrive with a few minutes to spare so you can get the drinks in before your tee time. With a big crowd, splitting into smaller teams keeps everyone playing and tends to fuel a bit of extra rivalry. Comfortable shoes are a good shout too, as you'll be on your feet for a while.

Newcastle is famous for its nightlife, but there's lots to see during the day as well. The Discovery Museum tells the story of Tyneside's inventions and industry, including Turbinia, once the fastest ship in the world, while the Great North Museum: Hancock has dinosaurs, Egyptian mummies and a planetarium. The Laing Art Gallery is another good stop for culture lovers.

Fancy some fresh air? Jesmond Dene is a leafy wooded valley in the city with waterfalls, bridges and a small farm, perfect for a stroll. The Ouseburn Valley is a creative quarter full of quirky pubs, music venues and the Seven Stories centre for children's books.

Football fans won't need telling that St James' Park sits right in the middle of the city, so expect busy streets on match days. Getting around is easy on the Tyne and Wear Metro, and the Angel of the North stands just outside the city at Gateshead if you fancy seeing the famous sculpture up close.
